question.leadin: Answer some questions about a famous American businessman who first became wealthy running a steamboat company.
question.text: This man, nicknamed "commodore," was awarded a Congressional Gold Medal for the donation of his namesake steamship to the Union Navy.
question.clue: This man served as a business manager for Thomas Gibbons before clashing with Daniel Drew over use of the Hudson River.

swap.leadin: Answer these questions about the Spanish-American War.
swap.text: One cause of the war was the supposed bombing of this U.S. ship that led to the slogan: "Remember the [blank]!"
swap.clue: In 1976 Hyman Rickover published a book questioning the long-held belief about the cause of its destruction, claiming that Captain Charles Sigsbee's poor supervision of the coal bunker was the real cause.

question.leadin: This man famously said "You may fire when you are ready" at a naval battle that he won in 1898.
question.text: Name this man, who led the American navy to victory at the Battle of Manila Bay.
question.clue: This man annihilated the fleet of Patricio Montojo y Pasaron by issuing the order "You may fire when you are ready, Gridley" while on board his flagship, the USS Olympia.

swap.leadin: Give the following about Native Americans in the United States.
swap.text: This law attempted to eliminate the Native American "communal" way of living by dividing tribal land into allotments of 160 acres for families and 80 acres for individuals.
swap.clue: This 1887 act allowed the U.S. government to survey Indian tribal lands and divide them up among the individuals in the tribe to assimilate Indians into American society.

question.text: Two years prior, German U-boats sank the Lusitania, which caused this Secretary of State to resign. This former populist presidential candidate claimed "you shall not crucify mankind" upon the title object in one speech.
question.clue: Just before he died, this person tried to uphold Tennessee's Butler Act by arguing a case against John Scopes, who was represented by Clarence Darrow.

swap.text: During the Homestead Strike, this industrialist hired Pinkerton agents to violently occupy the Homestead Steel Works. Following the Homestead Strike, Alexander Berkman attempted to assassinate this industrialist.
swap.clue: Joseph Duveen advised this man on purchasing works like Vermeer's Officer and Laughing Girl for his Fifth Avenue mansion.

question.text: Note to Moderator: Be generous on pronunciation. While Robert Todd Lincoln was outside the Temple of Music at the 1901 Pan-American Exposition in Buffalo, New York, this anarchist shot William McKinley.
question.clue: This immigrant, a disciple of the anarchist Emma Goldman, traveled to Buffalo and shot William McKinley in a reception line at the 1901 Pan-American Exposition.

swap.text: After President Garfield was shot, this Scottish-American inventor attempted to use his newly-invented metal detector to find the bullet. He is better known for having said the phrase "Mr. Watson-Come here-I want to see you."
swap.clue: This scientist's father developed the Visible Speech system, which he heavily advocated and taught to students at his school for the deaf.

question.text: He led a faction called the Liberal Republicans against Ulysses Grant, leading to his nomination for President by the Democrats on a ticket with Benjamin Gratz in 1872. For 15 points-name this founding editor of the New York Tribune.
question.clue: He died a broken man, having lost his most prized business venture to Whitelaw Reid.

swap.leadin: This movement had two phases, both started by Nevada Paiute.
swap.text: Wodziwob and Wovoka were the leaders of what religious revival among Plains Indians, which promised an end to white supremacy if certain movements were performed?
swap.clue: "Garments" in the Book of Mormon may have inspired the belief that clothes worn by this movement's adherents would gain resistance to bullets.

question.leadin: Identify the following people connected with a certain strike.
question.text: The strike got ugly when the National Guard was called out under this general, who would later distinguish himself by leading the invasion of Puerto Rico in the Spanish-American War and capturing Geronimo.
question.clue: His other notable success was shared with Oliver Otis Howard and saw its climax at Bear Paw ravine.

swap.text: Since you are a "disgruntled office seeker," your killing of Garfield prompts the 1883 passage of this piece of legislation meant to reform the civil service.
swap.clue: To prevent more Guiteau-like instances, Arthur signed this act. Named for an Ohio senator, it sought to eliminate the influence of political ties on government appointments.

question.leadin: Name some guys who have served as governor of New York in the 19th century.
question.text: This Governor of New York also served as Secretary of State and helped resolve the dispute over the Alabama Claims, along with helping his President attempt to annex the Dominican Republic.
question.clue: This name was held by a cabinet official who organized a plan to annex the Dominican Republic that was torpedoed by Charles Sumner.

swap.leadin: This book increased sympathy for poor immigrants by arguing that the squalor in which they lived was more a result of social forces than of personal immorality.
swap.text: Name this 1892 Jacob Riis (reese) book, which used photographs to illustrate the awful conditions in the overcrowded tenements of New York's slums.
swap.clue: This book contains a model colored map dividing its subject city into various ethnicities, and notes that the law defines its subject as "occupied by three or more families, living independently and doing their cooking on the premises."

question.leadin: Public outrage over this practice in New York City led to a 1788 riot during which John Jay was reportedly hit over the head with a rock.
question.text: Name this practice that inspired the passage of "bone bills" in several states, as introduced by the president of the American Chemical Society, John William Draper.
question.answerHtml: body snatching [accept equivalents like stealing corpses or digging up bodies; or cadaver research; prompt on grave robbing or stealing by asking “what objects were stolen?”]

swap.leadin: Answer the following about traditional and revivalist religions among Native Americans.
swap.text: Joseph Epes Brown collected descriptions of seven Oglala religious rites from this holy man. More famously, John Neihardt collected stories, ritual descriptions, and history of the Oglala into a work wherein this man "Speaks".

question.leadin: Description acceptable. Thomas Platt supported the creation of an inquiry committee for the realization of this goal that Andrew Haswell Green advanced.
question.text: Name this political goal achieved in 1898 to combat the growth in importance of Chicago. This goal paved the way for a construction project of William Barclay Parsons and a transit company called the IRT.
question.answerHtml: consolidation of the Boroughs [or equivalents like union of the Boroughs; or founding of the City of Greater New York; accept consolidation of New York City; reject descriptions like “founding of New York City” or “founding of Manhattan”]

swap.leadin: Answer some questions about anti-Mormon actions in American history.
swap.text: In this 1878 case, the Supreme Court ruled that bigamy as a Mormon religious duty was not protected under the First Amendment.
swap.clue: The Poland Act led to this 1878 test case, with a majority written by Chief Justice Morrison Waite. The Church allowed a man to be charged with bigamy; the Court upheld laws against polygamy against the argument that they infringed upon religious duty.

question.leadin: Name these exploring expeditions in the American West.
question.text: This geologist led a 10-year study of the 40th Parallel starting in Colorado, where he used his understanding of geology to blow the lid on the Diamond Hoax of 1872. Later in life, he passed as a black Pullman Porter named James Todd in order to marry Ada Copeland.

swap.text: This frontierswoman also joined the Wild West show, but her fame was mostly due to her being a character in the Deadwood Dick dime novels, which made her an icon of the Wild West. While considered a fierce fighter, this woman was renowned for her kindness and for aiding strangers in need.
swap.clue: This sharpshooter briefly joined Buffalo Bill's Wild West show, but left because of alcoholism. The dime novels of Edward Wheeler popularized the myth of this figure's connection to Deadwood Dick.
